name: crc_clmul
prose: Extends the running CRC crc over the len bytes at p using carry-less multiplication, with the constants in consts (crc-clmul-template.h:195-265; the packet slice was only its tail, and the function is named crc_clmul, not crc_clmul_update). If p is not aligned to sizeof(unsigned long) and len is non-zero, it first processes min(sizeof(unsigned long) - misalignment, len) leading bytes with crc_clmul_update_partial. If at least 4 words then remain it loads two words, folds across two words in a loop (while at least 2 words remain), reduces the two accumulators with crc_clmul_long and crc_clmul_update_long, and so consumes pairs of words. Remaining whole words (len >= sizeof(unsigned long)) are consumed one at a time with crc_clmul_update_long, and any final len % sizeof(unsigned long) bytes with crc_clmul_update_partial. It returns the resulting CRC; it only reads p, retains no reference to p or consts, and takes no locks.
note: Slice cut the head; real function crc_clmul at crc-clmul-template.h:195-265 read in full. Old prose described only the whole-word and tail steps (255-262) and omitted the alignment head and the 4-word fold loop (205-253).

name: chacha20poly1305_init
prose: Precondition: none; the function is invoked once at module load and needs no caller state. Postcondition: it returns 0, or it returns -19 (the numeric value of -ENODEV) exactly when CONFIG_CRYPTO_SELFTESTS is enabled and chacha20poly1305_selftest() returns false, in which case a WARN_ON warning is also emitted; no other return values are possible.
note: Read chacha20poly1305.c:359-365: returns -ENODEV when CONFIG_CRYPTO_SELFTESTS is enabled and WARN_ON(!chacha20poly1305_selftest()) fires (the warning is emitted), else 0. Prose correct, kept; old contract dropped (the function calls the selftest, which has side effects, and the contract was mechanically rejected).

name: mpihelp_lshift
prose: Precondition: cnt is strictly between 0 and BITS_PER_MPI_LIMB, usize is positive, up points to an array of at least usize limbs, wp points to an array of at least usize limbs, and if the destination overlaps the source then wp is at or above up. Postcondition: the function stores the shifted value at wp with the least significant destination limb wp[0] equal to up[0] << cnt and every other destination limb wp[i] (for 1 <= i <= usize-1) equal to (up[i] << cnt) | (up[i-1] >> (BITS_PER_MPI_LIMB - cnt)), and returns the bits shifted out of the most significant source limb, namely up[usize-1] >> (BITS_PER_MPI_LIMB - cnt), so result is strictly less than 2^cnt; no locks, references or memory are acquired or released by the caller.
note: Read generic_mpih-lshift.c:27-50. Reviewer claims (round 1 and 2: the prose swaps limbs) do not apply to the current prose: wp[0] = up[0] << cnt and wp[i] = (up[i] << cnt) | (up[i-1] >> (BITS_PER_MPI_LIMB - cnt)), returning up[usize-1] >> (BITS_PER_MPI_LIMB - cnt), match the loop at 42-47 with wp advanced by one. Prose kept.

name: bunzip2
prose: Decompresses a complete bzip2 stream (decompress_bunzip2.c:680-745). error must be a valid (non-NULL) callback: it is called with "Could not allocate output buffer", "Could not allocate input buffer", "Data integrity error when decompressing." and "Compressed file ends unexpectedly". If flush is non-NULL, the caller outbuf is ignored and an internal BZIP2_IOBUF_SIZE buffer is malloc'd; otherwise outbuf must be large enough for the whole decompressed output, because read_bunzip writes up to BZIP2_IOBUF_SIZE bytes per call and outbuf advances by the bytes written. If buf is non-NULL it must hold len bytes of input, otherwise an internal BZIP2_IOBUF_SIZE input buffer is malloc'd (and filled through fill, which may be NULL only if buf holds all the data). If the output buffer is NULL it calls error and returns RETVAL_OUT_OF_MEMORY; if the input buffer allocation fails it calls error, frees the output buffer if it allocated it, and returns RETVAL_OUT_OF_MEMORY. Otherwise it calls start_bunzip (which can return RETVAL_OUT_OF_MEMORY or RETVAL_NOT_BZIP_DATA without calling error) and then loops on read_bunzip; with flush set it passes each chunk to flush and, if flush writes fewer bytes than requested, stops with RETVAL_UNEXPECTED_OUTPUT_EOF and calls error. If read_bunzip ends with RETVAL_LAST_BLOCK it returns RETVAL_OK when headerCRC equals totalCRC and otherwise leaves RETVAL_LAST_BLOCK and calls error. Any other negative read_bunzip result (for example RETVAL_UNEXPECTED_INPUT_EOF, RETVAL_DATA_ERROR, RETVAL_OBSOLETE_INPUT) is returned unchanged without calling error. On every return after allocation it frees what it allocated (bd and its dbuf, the input buffer when buf was NULL, the output buffer when flush was non-NULL), and when pos is non-NULL and bd exists it stores bd->inbufPos in *pos.
note: Read decompress_bunzip2.c:630-745 and the RETVAL definitions. Reviewer claims all RIGHT: round-1 (error callback must be non-NULL), round-2 (outbuf must hold the whole output), round-15 (a stream ending early is RETVAL_UNEXPECTED_INPUT_EOF from read_bunzip, propagated unchanged without the error callback; only a short flush write gives RETVAL_UNEXPECTED_OUTPUT_EOF, line 717). The old first-sentence claim of UNEXPECTED_OUTPUT_EOF for an early stream end was wrong.

name: glob_init
prose: Precondition: none; glob_tests is a compile-time constant table that the function reads without caller-supplied inputs. Postcondition: runs every self-test in glob_tests, printing a per-test diagnostic for each failing test (and for each passing test when the verbose module parameter is set) plus one summary line, and returns 0 if every self-test passed or -ECANCELED (-125) if at least one self-test failed; the caller gains no memory, references or locks.
note: Read globtest.c:129-158: loops over glob_tests, counts successes, prints the summary with printk, returns -ECANCELED if any test failed else 0. Prose correct, kept; the old contract was rejected and the function prints, so it was dropped.

name: __sw_hweight64
prose: Precondition: w may be any 64-bit unsigned value (no restrictions). Postcondition: the function returns the Hamming weight of w, i.e. the total number of bits set in w, a value between 0 and 64, and it has no other effects on memory, locks or references.
note: Read hweight.c:47-67: the 32-bit build sums two __sw_hweight32 halves; the 64-bit build uses the standard bit-count reduction (multiply variant with CONFIG_ARCH_HAS_FAST_MULTIPLIER). Prose correct, kept. A weak but true contract bounds the result; the old giant contract was rejected by testing at w=65536, whose cause I could not determine from this source (the visible code returns a bit count); the new contract is only a bound.

name: LZ4_compress_generic
prose: Precondition: source is readable for inputSize bytes, inputSize is any int (a value outside 0..LZ4_MAX_INPUT_SIZE, including a negative one, makes the function return 0 at once, lz4_compress.c:206-208), maxOutputSize is non-negative, dest is writable for maxOutputSize bytes when outputLimited == limitedOutput and for LZ4_compressBound(inputSize) bytes when outputLimited == notLimited, source and dest do not overlap, dictPtr->hashTable is writable for the table size implied by tableType, and dictPtr->dictionary, dictSize and currentOffset describe a valid dictionary consistent with dict and dictIssue (with dictionary readable for dictSize bytes when dict is withPrefix64k or usingExtDict). Postcondition: it returns 0 without a usable compressed result if tableType == byU16 and inputSize >= LZ4_64Klimit, or if outputLimited == limitedOutput and the compressed output (including the all-literals fallback for inputSize < LZ4_minLength) would not fit in maxOutputSize; otherwise it writes the compressed representation of source to dest, returns the positive number of bytes written (at most maxOutputSize when outputLimited == limitedOutput and at most LZ4_compressBound(inputSize) when outputLimited == notLimited), and for inputs that pass the size checks and have inputSize >= LZ4_minLength it updates entries in dictPtr->hashTable while searching (shorter inputs and early size-check failures do not update the hash table, but hash-table updates may already have occurred when a later limitedOutput check returns 0); on a limitedOutput failure dest may have been partially written, and the function takes no locks and allocates or frees no memory.
note: Slice cut the head; real function LZ4_compress_generic at lz4_compress.c:175-455. Returns verified at 208, 230, 310, 371, 436 (all 0) and 454 (op - dest). Reviewer round-1 claim (notLimited can write more than maxOutputSize) and round-2 claim (hash table not updated when inputSize < LZ4_minLength) are RIGHT and are already in the prose. I did not check every path of the match loop in detail.

name: RAID6_RVV_WRAPPER(_n)
prose: Generated by RAID6_RVV_WRAPPER(_n) (rvv.h:10-39), instantiated for _n = 1, 2, 4 and 8, as the static function raid6_rvv<_n>_gen_syndrome(int disks, size_t bytes, void **ptrs): it calls kernel_vector_begin(), then raid6_rvv<_n>_gen_syndrome_real(disks, (unsigned long)bytes, ptrs), then kernel_vector_end(), and returns nothing. The called function treats ptrs as disks buffer pointers with the data blocks at indexes 0 to disks-3, the P (XOR parity) buffer at ptrs[disks-2] and the Q (RS syndrome) buffer at ptrs[disks-1], and writes P and Q for the bytes processed (bytes is stepped in NSIZE-sized vector chunks). The wrapper itself checks no argument.
note: Macro-generated wrapper named by its definition head per rule 5. Read rvv.h:10-39 and raid6/rvv.c:23-50 (real function: z0 = disks - 3, p = dptr[z0 + 1], q = dptr[z0 + 2]). Old prose spoke of 'P and Q ... for the disks data blocks', i.e. data count = disks, which is wrong: disks includes the P and Q buffers.

name: RAID6_RVV_WRAPPER(_n)
prose: Generated by RAID6_RVV_WRAPPER(_n) (rvv.h:10-39), instantiated for _n = 1, 2, 4 and 8, as the static function raid6_rvv<_n>_xor_syndrome(int disks, int start, int stop, size_t bytes, void **ptrs): it calls kernel_vector_begin(), then raid6_rvv<_n>_xor_syndrome_real(disks, start, stop, (unsigned long)bytes, ptrs), then kernel_vector_end(), and returns nothing. The called function treats ptrs as disks buffer pointers with the P buffer at ptrs[disks-2] and the Q buffer at ptrs[disks-1]; it starts from data block ptrs[stop] (z0 = stop), so stop must be a valid data block index (at most disks-3) and start must not exceed stop; it updates P and Q for changes in the data blocks from start to stop inclusive. The wrapper itself checks no argument.
note: Macro-generated wrapper named by its definition head per rule 5. Read rvv.h:10-39 and raid6/rvv.c:95-105 (z0 = stop, p = dptr[disks - 2], q = dptr[disks - 1]). Reviewer round-15 claim (the old precondition allows stop = disks, which would read out of bounds) is RIGHT: the corrected bound is stop <= disks - 3. The old prose said the range [start, stop) is covered; the real function indexes up to and including stop.

name: decode_rs8
prose: Reed-Solomon decoder body (lib/reed_solomon/decode_rs.c), which is not a function by itself: it is #included inside decode_rs8 and decode_rs16 in reed_solomon.c (decode_rs8(rsc, data, par, len, s, no_eras, eras_pos, invmsk, corr); the 16-bit version has the same logic). It computes pad = nn - nroots - len and BUG_ON()s if pad < 0 or pad >= nn - nroots. If the caller passed syndromes s (in index form) and every s[i] equals nn it returns 0 at once; otherwise it computes the syndromes from data and par (using invmsk) and returns 0 if they are all zero. It then builds the error locator polynomial lambda with the Berlekamp-Massey iteration (seeded from the no_eras erasure positions in eras_pos), finds its degree deg_lambda and returns -EBADMSG if deg_lambda is 0. It searches the field for the roots of lambda (Chien search); it returns -EBADMSG if a root maps to a position below pad (an impossible location) or if the number of roots differs from deg_lambda. It then computes the error values (omega polynomial) and, after computing them, recomputes the syndromes of the correction and returns -EBADMSG if any differs from the original. Otherwise, if corr and eras_pos are both non-NULL it stores the non-zero error values in corr and their positions (loc - pad) in eras_pos; else, if data and par are both non-NULL, it XORs the error values into data (locations below nn - nroots) or par; if neither pair is supplied the corrections are not applied. It returns num_corrected, the number of non-zero error values found. It uses the rs_control buffers and takes no locks.
note: decode_rs.c is a template body, not a named function: the real functions are decode_rs8 and decode_rs16 (reed_solomon.c:361-366, 412-). The packet item was the first slice (items 8 and 9 are the same body; rec 9 covers its tail). Read decode_rs.c:1-326 with returns/gotos (BUG_ON at 43, 0 at 56 and 102, -EBADMSG at 194, 213, 230 and 300, num_corrected at 325). Old prose said the return is the number of corrected symbols and that 0 means a zero syndrome (right) but missed the BUG_ON and the condition under which corrections are applied.

name: decode_rs8
prose: Last stage of the Reed-Solomon decoder body (lib/reed_solomon/decode_rs.c, #included in decode_rs8 and decode_rs16 in reed_solomon.c): after the error values b[j] have been computed for the count error locations loc[j], it recomputes the syndromes of that error pattern and returns -EBADMSG if any recomputed syndrome differs from the original s[i] (nothing has been written to data, par, corr or eras_pos before this check). If the check passes and corr and eras_pos are both non-NULL it stores the non-zero error values in corr and their positions (loc - pad) in eras_pos; otherwise, if data and par are both non-NULL, it XORs each error value into data[loc - pad] (for locations below nn - nroots) or par[loc - pad - len]; if neither pair of pointers is provided the corrections are not applied. It returns num_corrected, the number of non-zero error values.
note: Template body, not a named function (real functions decode_rs8/decode_rs16); this slice is lines 261-326 of decode_rs.c. Read 289-325 (recheck at 289-301 returns -EBADMSG; apply at 307-322; return at 325). Old prose said corrections 'applied to corr/eras_pos or data/par' without the dependency on which pointers are non-NULL and that nothing is written when the recheck fails.

name: encode_rs8
prose: Reed-Solomon encoder body (lib/reed_solomon/encode_rs.c), which is not a function by itself: it is #included inside encode_rs8 and encode_rs16 in reed_solomon.c (for example encode_rs8(rsc, data, len, par, invmsk)). It computes pad = nn - nroots - len and returns -ERANGE, leaving par untouched, if pad < 0 or pad >= nn. Otherwise for each of the len data symbols it XORs the symbol (with invmsk applied and masked by nn) with par[0] and takes index_of of the result as the feedback value fb, then (when fb is not nn) updates par[1..nroots-1] with the generator polynomial terms when the feedback is not nn, shifts par down by one symbol and puts the new last symbol in par[nroots-1]. par is therefore used as a running remainder register: it is read as well as written and must be initialised by the caller (all zero for a plain parity computation) before the first call. It returns 0 after the last symbol; it takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: encode_rs.c is a template body; the packet name encode_block is not defined anywhere. The real functions are encode_rs8 (reed_solomon.c:328-332) and encode_rs16 (381-). Read encode_rs.c:12-47. Old prose said par holds the remainder 'computed over data' but did not say par is also an input (par[0] is read at line 29); added. Rest of the old prose (the -ERANGE condition and untouched par) is correct.

name: dmirror_fops_unlocked_ioctl
prose: Precondition: filp is a valid open file for the dmirror driver (its private_data may be NULL) and arg is a user-space pointer to a buffer of at least sizeof(struct hmm_dmirror_cmd) bytes that is readable, and writable if the call is to complete with a copy-back. Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL if filp->private_data is NULL, -EFAULT if copy_from_user of the command fails, -EINVAL if cmd.addr is not page-aligned or cmd.addr >= cmd.addr + (cmd.npages << PAGE_SHIFT) or command is not one of the recognized HMM_DMIRROR_* values, and otherwise zeroes cmd.cpages and cmd.faults, dispatches to the matching handler (dmirror_read, dmirror_write, dmirror_migrate_to_device, dmirror_migrate_to_system, dmirror_exclusive, dmirror_check_atomic, dmirror_snapshot, or dmirror_device_remove_chunks with ret set to 0 for HMM_DMIRROR_RELEASE), returns the handler's nonzero error unchanged without copying back, and on handler success copies the updated cmd back to arg, returning 0 or -EFAULT if that copy_to_user fails.
note: Read test_hmm.c:1286-1355: -EINVAL for NULL private_data (before the copy), -EFAULT on copy_from_user failure, -EINVAL for a misaligned or wrapping address range, per-command handlers, HMM_DMIRROR_RELEASE removes the chunks and sets ret = 0, a non-zero handler result is returned without copy back, then copy_to_user (-EFAULT on failure). Reviewer claims (round 1: RELEASE can return -EFAULT; round 2: preconditions are validated, not assumed) RIGHT and already in the prose. Prose kept.

name: ot_mod_init
prose: Precondition: the static g_testcases table is initialized and ot_init_data, ot_start_sync and ot_start_async are callable. Postcondition: the function iterates over every entry of g_testcases, calling ot_init_data on each and then running it via ot_start_sync or ot_start_async (any failure such as -ENOMEM returned by ot_start_async is ignored and does not abort the loop), prints one summary line per testcase, and unconditionally returns -EAGAIN (-11) so module load always fails; the caller acquires no resources that need releasing.
note: Read test_objpool.c:648-671: runs every testcase (ot_start_async/ot_start_sync results are ignored), prints a summary, and returns -EAGAIN unconditionally. Prose correct, kept; old contract dropped (the function runs tests and prints, rule 4).

name: CREATE_WRAPPER(ffs)
prose: Generated function build_test_ffs(void) has no precondition: it declares int init_ffs = 32 and int result_ffs = ffs(6), passes both addresses to barrier_data() so the compiler cannot discard them, and returns true; BUILD_BUG_ON(init_ffs < 32) is a compile-time assertion that is false for the constant initial value 32 and has no run-time effect (init_ffs is an ordinary automatic variable; the source comment says the test is whether the initial value vanishes after the call). Postcondition: the function always returns true and has no other effect at run time.
note: Read ffs_kunit.c:505-518: the function is generated by CREATE_WRAPPER(ffs) as build_test_ffs. Reviewer round-15 claim (init_ffs is automatic, BUILD_BUG_ON cannot detect ffs clobbering it or check const) is RIGHT; prose corrected. The function returns true unconditionally.

name: DEFINE_ALLOC_SIZE_TEST_PAIR(kmalloc)
prose: Generated function fortify_test_alloc_size_kmalloc_const(struct kunit *test). Precondition: it is called as a KUnit test with a valid struct kunit *test, and CONST_TEST_BODY supplies the compile-time-constant sizes 0, 1, 128, 1023, 1025, 4096 and 4097 (the 0 case is skipped only for the vmalloc variant, so it does run here). Postcondition: it returns void and has no error code; for each size it runs TEST_kmalloc, which allocates with kmalloc, kmalloc_node, kzalloc, kzalloc_node, kcalloc(1,n), kcalloc(n,1), kcalloc_node(1,n), kcalloc_node(n,1), kmalloc_array(1,n), kmalloc_array(n,1), kmalloc_array_node(1,n), kmalloc_array_node(n,1), then krealloc and krealloc_array on a freshly kmalloc'd buffer with twice the size, and finally kmemdup("hello there", 11, gfp); for every one of these it asserts the returned pointer is non-NULL, asserts __builtin_object_size(p,1) equals the requested size (twice the size for the krealloc/krealloc_array cases) and, when the compiler has __builtin_dynamic_object_size, that __builtin_dynamic_object_size(p,1) equals the same value, then frees p with kfree; failed expectations only mark the KUnit test failed and never abort the function.
note: Read fortify_kunit.c:156-289 and 209-217: DEFINE_ALLOC_SIZE_TEST_PAIR(kmalloc) defines the _const and _dynamic tests; CONST_TEST_BODY runs sizes 0, 1, 128, 1023, 1025, 4096 and 4097 (the 0 case is skipped only when the allocator name is TEST_vmalloc), TEST_kmalloc runs the 12 allocation checks, then krealloc and two krealloc_array variants of a fresh kmalloc buffer with twice the size, and a kmemdup of 11 bytes. Prose correct, kept; the round-15 reviewer note about size++ applies only to the dynamic test.

name: DEFINE_ALLOC_SIZE_TEST_PAIR(kmalloc)
prose: Generated function fortify_test_alloc_size_kmalloc_dynamic(struct kunit *test). Precondition: it is called as a KUnit test with a valid struct kunit *test; if the compiler lacks __builtin_dynamic_object_size the body is a single kunit_skip and nothing else runs, otherwise size is initialized to the volatile unknown_size (50), and in each checker call expected_size is the value of size before the increment while alloc_size is size++ (the code relies on the documented -Wunsequenced behavior). Postcondition: it returns void and has no error code; when not skipped, TEST_kmalloc runs with expected_size = size and alloc_size = size++, so each of the 15 allocation checks (the 12 kmalloc-family calls plus krealloc and the two krealloc_array calls, the latter three with twice the size) allocates the current size, asserts the pointer is non-NULL, asserts __builtin_object_size(p,1) == SIZE_MAX and __builtin_dynamic_object_size(p,1) == the expected size, and frees p with kfree, while the final kmemdup uses len = 11 + zero_size (11 at run time); size is incremented 18 times (the three orig = kmalloc(alloc_size, gfp) lines before the krealloc and krealloc_array checks also evaluate size++, in addition to the 15 checker calls that precede the kmemdup), so the closing KUNIT_EXPECT_NE(test, size, unknown_size) holds; failed expectations only mark the KUnit test failed and never abort the function.
note: Read fortify_kunit.c:195-275. Reviewer round-15 claim (the orig = kmalloc(alloc_size) lines also consume size++, so size is incremented 18 times, not 15) is RIGHT (255, 260, 265). Macro-generated by DEFINE_ALLOC_SIZE_TEST_PAIR(kmalloc).

name: __fortify_test(memcpy)
prose: Generated function fortify_test_memcpy(test). Precondition: test is a valid KUnit test context and the zero-initialized pad/empty buffers and srcA/srcB arrays are usable stack objects. Postcondition: the function returns void after asserting that memcpy() with sizes 0, 1, len-1 and len succeeds with no fortify_read_overflows or fortify_write_overflows, that a copy of len+1 bytes into pad.buf and then a copy of len bytes into pad.buf + 1 each increment fortify_write_overflows, to 1 and 2 respectively, and that copying into the zero-length empty.buf with size 0 is silent while size 1 increments fortify_write_overflows to 1.
note: Read fortify_kunit.c:874-936: generated by __fortify_test(memcpy). The second overflow call is memfunc(pad.buf + 1, srcB, len) (921), not len+1; reviewer round-15 claim RIGHT; prose corrected.

name: __fortify_test(memmove)
prose: Generated function fortify_test_memmove(test). Precondition: test is a valid KUnit test context and the zero-initialized pad/empty buffers and srcA/srcB arrays are usable stack objects. Postcondition: the function returns void after asserting that memmove() with sizes 0, 1, len-1 and len succeeds with no fortify_read_overflows or fortify_write_overflows, that a copy of len+1 bytes into pad.buf and then a copy of len bytes into pad.buf + 1 each increment fortify_write_overflows, to 1 and 2 respectively, and that copying into the zero-length empty.buf with size 0 is silent while size 1 increments fortify_write_overflows to 1.
note: Read fortify_kunit.c:874-936: generated by __fortify_test(memmove); same body as memcpy with memmove. Second overflow call is len bytes at offset 1 (921); reviewer claim RIGHT; prose corrected.

name: next_step
prose: Precondition: the signed int arithmetic start+inc, end-inc, idx+inc and idx+1 must not overflow, i.e. start+inc, end-inc and idx+inc lie in the int range and idx <= 2147483646. Postcondition: after start is increased by inc and end is decreased by inc, if idx < start or idx+inc > end then the function sets inc to 1 and returns idx+1, otherwise it returns idx+inc.
contract: /*@ requires start + inc >= -2147483648 && start + inc <= 2147483647 && end - inc >= -2147483648 && end - inc <= 2147483647 && idx + inc >= -2147483648 && idx + inc <= 2147483647 && idx <= 2147483646; ensures result == ((idx < \old(start) + \old(inc) || idx + \old(inc) > \old(end) - \old(inc)) ? idx + 1 : idx + \old(inc)); */
note: Read memcpy_kunit.c:385-391: start += inc; end -= inc; if (idx < start || idx + inc > end) inc = 1; return idx + inc. Prose correct, kept. The old contract used the modified start, end and inc in its ensures, which is why random testing falsified it; the contract below uses \old values and the overflow-freedom requirements of the prose.

name: DEFINE_TEST_FUNC(u8, "%d")
prose: Generated function u8_u8__u8_overflow_test(test). Precondition: test is a valid kunit test context and the static table u8_u8__u8_tests holds its 3 test vectors. Postcondition: the SKIP_64_ON_32 and SKIP_SIGN_MISMATCH guards are false for u8 so no skip occurs; the function iterates over all 3 vectors calling do_test_u8_u8__u8, which uses KUNIT_EXPECT_* assertions to verify that check_{add,sub,mul}_overflow, wrapping_{add,sub,mul} and wrapping_assign_{add,sub} yield the expected overflow flags and results and have no macro side-effects, then logs the vector count via kunit_info and returns normally, acquiring or releasing no locks, references or memory.
note: Read overflow_kunit.c:253-362: generated by DEFINE_TEST_FUNC(u8, "%d") through DEFINE_TEST_FUNC_TYPED, which defines do_test_u8_u8__u8 (check_one_op for add, sub, mul in both operand orders, check_self_op for assign_add and assign_sub) and u8_u8__u8_overflow_test (skip macros, loop over the vectors, kunit_info). Prose correct, kept.

name: DO_MANY_MEMBERS(func_body)
prose: Precondition: none; the int argument is ignored and the function has no side effects. Postcondition: it returns offsetof(struct randstruct_funcs_untouched, a), which is 0 because a is the first member of a struct marked __no_randomize_layout, on every return path; the caller acquires and releases nothing.
note: Read randstruct_kunit.c:60-65: func_a is generated by func_body(a, ...) via DO_MANY_MEMBERS(func_body); it returns offsetof(struct randstruct_funcs_untouched, a), which is 0 for the first member of a __no_randomize_layout struct, and ignores its argument. Prose correct, kept.

name: fsm_find
prose: Precondition: conf and state are valid pointers, ts_config_priv(conf) is a struct ts_fsm with ntokens >= 1 and a valid tokens array in which no token with recur == TS_FSM_HEAD_IGNORE is the last token, and conf->get_next_block(consumed, &data, conf, state) returns the number of octets in the data block starting at octet offset consumed (0 once the data is exhausted) and stores a pointer to that block in data. Postcondition: the scan is strict iff tokens[0].recur != TS_FSM_HEAD_IGNORE; in strict mode a mismatch of a SINGLE, MULTI or ANY token returns UINT_MAX at once, while in non-strict mode the leading HEAD_IGNORE token skips octets until the second token matches (returning UINT_MAX if an octet matches neither the first nor the second token) and a mismatch of a later SINGLE, MULTI or ANY token restarts the scan from the octet after the mismatching octet, while a PERHAPS token that does not match is simply skipped (the loop continues with the next token); a match is reported only when the token sequence is fully consumed and, if the last token is SINGLE or PERHAPS, the data ends at the position reached by the scan, in which case result is the offset of the first octet of the match (match_start, updated by any HEAD_IGNORE skip) and state->offset is set to the offset just past the last octet consumed by the match; otherwise result is UINT_MAX and fsm_find does not modify state->offset.
note: Read ts_fsm.c:135-253. Reviewer claims: round-1 (strict mode) RIGHT and in prose; round-15 (a PERHAPS mismatch just continues, 182-185) RIGHT; prose corrected. The match test (after all tokens, data must end unless the last token is MULTI/ANY, lines 244-245 and 199-200) matches the prose.

name: zlib_deflate
prose: Precondition: strm->state, when non-NULL, points to a deflate_state initialized by zlib_deflateInit* or zlib_deflateReset, and callers supply strm->next_in non-NULL whenever strm->avail_in is nonzero and, once the status is FINISH_STATE, call only with flush == Z_FINISH and avail_in == 0 (violations are reported as errors rather than undefined behavior). Postcondition: it returns Z_STREAM_ERROR without modifying the state if strm or strm->state is NULL, flush is outside 0..Z_FINISH, strm->next_in is NULL while strm->avail_in is nonzero, or the status is FINISH_STATE and flush is not Z_FINISH; Z_BUF_ERROR if strm->avail_out is 0 on entry, or if s->pending == 0 and strm->avail_in == 0 and flush is not Z_FINISH and flush is not greater than the previous call's flush value, or, after any pending output has been flushed (a flush that leaves avail_out at 0 returns Z_OK first, deflate.c:373-384), if the status is FINISH_STATE and strm->avail_in is nonzero; otherwise it stores strm in s->strm and flush in s->last_flush, emits the zlib header when the status is INIT_STATE, consumes input and produces pending output, and returns Z_OK, except that with flush == Z_FINISH it writes the adler32 trailer (unless headerless), flushes pending output, marks the trailer written, and returns Z_STREAM_END when s->pending is 0 or Z_OK when pending output remains, and in the Z_OK paths where strm->avail_out became 0 while flushing pending output or processing a block it sets s->last_flush to -1 so the caller must repeat the call with the same flush parameter.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function zlib_deflate at deflate.c:326-469. Reviewer claims round-2 (Z_BUF_ERROR requires s->pending == 0, 390-392) and round-15 (FINISH_STATE with avail_in nonzero yields Z_BUF_ERROR only after the pending flush did not exhaust avail_out, 373-398) are RIGHT; round-2 was already in the prose, round-15 is now added.

name: zlib_inflate
prose: Precondition: strm is non-NULL, strm->state points to an inflate_state already initialized by zlib_inflateInit/inflateReset, strm->next_in/avail_in and strm->next_out/avail_out describe the caller's input and output buffers (next_in may be NULL only when avail_in is 0), and flush is the caller's flush request (e.g. Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_BLOCK, Z_FINISH, Z_PACKET_FLUSH). Postcondition: the function decodes deflate data, consuming input and producing output, and returns Z_STREAM_ERROR (leaving strm untouched) if strm or strm->state is NULL, next_in is NULL with avail_in nonzero, or the state mode is SYNC or unrecognized; Z_NEED_DICT after saving the bit buffer and stream positions back into strm when a preset dictionary is required and none was supplied; Z_MEM_ERROR when the state mode is MEM; Z_DATA_ERROR with strm->msg set when the header, stored-block, code-length, literal/length, distance or data-check data is invalid; Z_STREAM_END when the final block and check value have been verified; Z_BUF_ERROR when the result would otherwise be Z_OK but no input was consumed and no output produced, or flush == Z_FINISH; and Z_OK when the stream is not yet complete; on every return other than the early Z_STREAM_ERROR, Z_NEED_DICT, Z_MEM_ERROR (mode MEM) and SYNC or unrecognized-mode Z_STREAM_ERROR returns (which return directly, bypassing inf_leave and its write-back) the bit buffer and stream positions are written back to strm, strm->total_in, strm->total_out and strm->data_type are updated, the window is updated when needed, and strm->adler/state->check are updated when checksumming is enabled and output was produced; when flush == Z_PACKET_FLUSH, the provisional result is Z_OK, strm->avail_out != 0 and strm->avail_in == 0, the function instead returns the result of zlib_inflateSyncPacket(strm) after the totals and checksum have been updated; no memory ownership changes hands and the caller retains ownership of all buffers.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function zlib_inflate at inflate.c:331-767 (tail at 742-767). Reviewer round-15 claim (the MEM and SYNC/default returns bypass inf_leave, so bit buffer and positions are not written back) is RIGHT (730-734); prose corrected.

name: zlib_inflateIncomp
prose: Adds the data at z->next_in / z->avail_in to the inflate history window without producing output (inflate.c:785-814); the stream state must be waiting at the start of a block. It returns Z_DATA_ERROR, changing nothing, if the state mode is neither TYPE nor HEAD. Otherwise it temporarily sets avail_out to 0 and next_out to the end of the input, calls zlib_updatewindow for avail_in bytes, restores next_out and avail_out, updates z->adler and state->check with UPDATE over the input, then increases z->total_out, z->total_in and state->total by the old avail_in, advances next_in past the input, sets avail_in to 0 and returns Z_OK.
note: Packet item was an unnamed tail; the real function is zlib_inflateIncomp (inflate.c:785-814, head read at 785-806). Old prose described only the counters (807-813) and omitted the Z_DATA_ERROR return for a wrong state mode, the window update, and the checksum update.

name: zlib_inflate_table
prose: Precondition: type is CODES, LENS, or DISTS, lens[0..codes-1] holds the code lengths each in 0..MAXBITS, work points to at least codes unsigned shorts of scratch space, *table points to a buffer with room for at least ENOUGH code entries, and *bits is the requested root table index bits. Postcondition: the function returns 0 after building the decoding table(s) — in the no-symbols case (max == 0) it writes two invalid-code entries, sets *bits to 1 and advances *table by 2, otherwise it fills the root table and any sub-tables (marking unused entries of an incomplete code invalid), advances *table past the used entries and sets *bits to the root table's index-bit count — returns -1 if the code lengths are over-subscribed or form an incomplete set (except that a single-symbol LENS or DISTS code is accepted), and returns 1 if for type LENS the accumulated table size would reach ENOUGH - MAXD entries, with *table and *bits left unchanged on every failure return and the buffer untouched for the -1 and initial 1 returns but possibly partially written for the in-loop 1 return.
note: Read inftrees.c (zlib_inflate_table): returns 0 for no symbols after writing two invalid entries (103-110); -1 for over-subscribed (121) or an incomplete set (123-124, a single-symbol LENS/DISTS code excepted); 1 for LENS when the size would reach ENOUGH - MAXD (198, 266); *table and *bits updated only at the end (312-313). Prose correct, kept.

name: HUF_writeCTable_wksp
prose: Precondition: dst is a writable buffer of maxDstSize bytes, CTable is a valid HUF_CElt table whose header records exactly maxSymbolValue and huffLog, and workspace points to workspaceSize writable bytes (at least sizeof(HUF_WriteCTableWksp) after alignment). Postcondition: returns the number of bytes written to dst (1 + the FSE-compressed weight size when that size is >1 and < maxSymbolValue/2, otherwise 1 + (maxSymbolValue+1)/2 bytes of raw 4-bit weights), or an error code: ERROR(GENERIC) when the aligned workspace is smaller than sizeof(HUF_WriteCTableWksp), ERROR(maxSymbolValue_tooLarge) when maxSymbolValue > HUF_SYMBOLVALUE_MAX, ERROR(dstSize_tooSmall) when maxDstSize < 1, the error returned by HUF_compressWeights, and, only when the FSE-compressed form was not chosen, ERROR(GENERIC) when maxSymbolValue > 128 and ERROR(dstSize_tooSmall) when the raw-weight output does not fit.
note: Slice cut the head; real function HUF_writeCTable_wksp at huf_compress.c:246-287. Reviewer round-15 claim (the maxSymbolValue > 128 ERROR(GENERIC) is not unconditional: the FSE path can return success first, 274-277 before 280) is RIGHT; ordered conditions now stated.

name: ZSTD_compressContinue_internal
prose: Precondition: cctx is a ZSTD_CCtx initialized for compression whose stage is not ZSTDcs_created, dst points to dstCapacity writable bytes and src to srcSize readable bytes. Postcondition: it returns the stage_wrong error without writing anything when cctx->stage is ZSTDcs_created; otherwise, when frame is nonzero and the stage was ZSTDcs_init it first writes the frame header (fhSize bytes, advancing dst and dstCapacity and setting the stage to ZSTDcs_ongoing, propagating any ZSTD_writeFrameHeader error) and then, if srcSize is 0, returns fhSize without compressing, without updating the match-state or LDM windows and without changing consumedSrcSize or producedCSize; otherwise it updates the match-state window (and the LDM window when LDM is enabled), performs overflow correction when frame is 0, compresses the chunk with ZSTD_compress_frameChunk or ZSTD_compressBlock_internal (propagating its error, in which case the counters are not updated), then adds srcSize to consumedSrcSize and cSize+fhSize to producedCSize and returns cSize+fhSize, except that when pledgedSrcSizePlusOne is nonzero and consumedSrcSize+1 exceeds it, it returns the srcSize_wrong error after the output and counters have already been updated; in every error case some bytes may already have been written to dst, so the caller must treat dst as invalid, and the function takes no lock and acquires no reference, the caller retaining ownership of cctx, dst and src.
note: Read zstd_compress.c:4706-4765 (head at 4706-4718 not re-listed): -stage_wrong before any write (stage ZSTDcs_created), frame header write and stage change (4719-4727), srcSize == 0 returns fhSize with no counter or window update (4729), window updates, overflow correction only for frame == 0, cSize errors forwarded before the counters are updated (4750-4752), srcSize_wrong check after the counters are updated (4754-4762), return cSize + fhSize. Reviewer claims (round-1 output may already be written; round-2 fhSize not added to producedCSize on srcSize == 0) are RIGHT and already in the prose. Prose kept.

name: ZSTD_compressStream_generic
prose: Precondition: zcs is a valid ZSTD_CStream already initialized for streaming compression, input and output are valid ZSTD_inBuffer/ZSTD_outBuffer descriptors with pos <= size (and size == 0 when src/dst is NULL), flushMode is ZSTD_e_continue, ZSTD_e_flush or ZSTD_e_end, and in stable-buffer modes the buffers match the expectations recorded by the previous call. Postcondition: on success input->pos and output->pos are advanced by the bytes consumed and produced, the stream state advances (in stable input mode with ZSTD_e_continue, bytes not yet compressed are reported as consumed and recorded in zcs->stableIn_notConsumed to be re-read from the same buffer on the next call), and the function returns 0 when the frame has been completed (the session then being reset for a new frame) or otherwise a positive hint of the input size expected by the next call, while on error it returns a non-zero ZSTD error code (ZSTD_error_init_missing if the stream was never initialized, or an error forwarded from the internal compression pass such as dstSizeTooSmall) and returns immediately, leaving input->pos and output->pos un-updated except that input->pos was first reduced by the previous stableIn_notConsumed (which is reset to 0) and recording no new stableIn_notConsumed.
note: Read zstd_compress.c:5989-6172 (and the error paths). Prose matches: stableIn_notConsumed is subtracted from input->pos and reset at entry (6006-6009); ZSTD_error_init_missing for zcss_init (6028-6029); errors from the internal compression forwarded immediately, before input->pos and output->pos are stored (6169-6170); return 0 when frameEnded else ZSTD_nextInputSizeHint (6171-6172). Reviewer round-2 claim (on error the positions are not updated) RIGHT and already stated. Prose kept; I did not trace every stable-buffer branch.

name: ZSTD_RowFindBestMatch
prose: Row-hash match finder (zstd_lazy.c:1142-1335; the packet slice was only its tail): it searches the row-based hash table of match state ms for the longest match of the data at ip, limited to iLimit, for the match-state window and, depending on dictMode, the external or dictionary match state. It starts with ml = 4 - 1 = 3 and replaces it only when it finds a match longer than the current ml; only then does it write the offset code OFFSET_TO_OFFBASE(distance) through *offsetPtr. It returns ml: the length of the best match found, or 3 when no match longer than 3 was found (not 0), in which case *offsetPtr is left unchanged. It examines at most 2^searchLog entries (nbAttempts, capped by the row size) per table, may also search the dictionary match state (including the dedicated dictionary search), and may update row-hash tags and the next-update position of ms as a side effect.
note: Slice cut the head; real function ZSTD_RowFindBestMatch at zstd_lazy.c:1142-1335. Old prose said it returns 0 if no match; the code initialises size_t ml = 4-1 (1171) and returns ml (1334), so the no-match value is 3. Side effects on ms (tag and nextToUpdate updates) are from the earlier part of the function that I only skimmed.

name: GEN_ZSTD_BT_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls)
prose: Macro-generated family of match-search wrapper functions in zstd_lazy.c:1366-1395, instantiated for each dictMode and mls. GEN_ZSTD_BT_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls) defines ZSTD_BT_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls)(ms, ip, iLimit, offBasePtr), which returns ZSTD_BtFindBestMatch(ms, ip, iLimit, offBasePtr, mls, ZSTD_<dictMode>); GEN_ZSTD_HC_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls) likewise defines ZSTD_HC_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls) returning ZSTD_HcFindBestMatch(..., mls, ZSTD_<dictMode>); GEN_ZSTD_ROW_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls, rowLog) defines ZSTD_ROW_SEARCH_FN(dictMode, mls, rowLog) returning ZSTD_RowFindBestMatch(..., mls, ZSTD_<dictMode>, rowLog). Each wrapper begins with assert statements (active only in debug builds) that MAX(4, MIN(6, ms->cParams.minMatch)) equals the template mls (and for the row version that MAX(4, MIN(6, ms->cParams.searchLog)) equals rowLog); it returns the wrapped finder result unchanged, including whatever it writes through the offset pointer.
note: Macro-generated family named by the BT definition head per rule 5; read zstd_lazy.c:1362-1395. Old precondition said minMatch and searchLog must equal the template constants; in the code that is only an assert (1372, 1382, 1392-1393), so it is not an enforced precondition.

name: ZSTD_compressBlock_greedy_row
prose: Precondition: ms, seqStore and rep point to a valid match state, sequence store and repcode array, and [src, src+srcSize) is a readable block consistent with ms's window. Postcondition: the call is forwarded verbatim to ZSTD_compressBlock_lazy_generic with searchMethod search_rowHash, depth 0 and dictMode ZSTD_noDict, which appends the parsed sequences to seqStore, writes the two final repcode offsets into rep[0] and rep[1] (rep[2] is left unchanged), updates ms->nextToUpdate and ms->lazySkipping (ms->window is not modified), and whose return value — the number of trailing last-literal bytes of the block not covered by any emitted sequence, not the number of bytes consumed — is returned unchanged.
note: Read zstd_lazy.c:1806-1811 (forwards to ZSTD_compressBlock_lazy_generic with search_rowHash, depth 0, ZSTD_noDict) and the end of the generic function (rep[0] and rep[1] written at 326-327 in the generic body, rep[2] untouched; ms->lazySkipping assigned at 119 and 175; returns iend - anchor at 330). Reviewer claims (return is the last-literals size; rep[2] not written) are RIGHT and already in the prose. Prose kept.

name: ZSTD_estimateDStreamSize
prose: Precondition: none; any size_t windowSize is accepted. Postcondition: letting B = min(windowSize, ZSTD_BLOCKSIZE_MAX) and R = windowSize + 2*B + 64 computed in unsigned long long arithmetic (wrapping modulo 2^64 on overflow), if (size_t)R != R the helper ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min returns the frameParameter_windowTooLarge error code as outBuffSize, which ZSTD_estimateDStreamSize does not check, so the function returns the size_t sum ZSTD_estimateDCtxSize() + B + that error-code value (wrapped), not an error code itself; otherwise it returns ZSTD_estimateDCtxSize() + B + (size_t)R computed in size_t arithmetic (wrapping modulo SIZE_MAX+1 on overflow), and in either case it acquires or releases no locks, references or memory.
note: Read zstd_decompress.c:1895-1922. Reviewer round-2 claim (the internal helper can return frameParameter_windowTooLarge) is RIGHT; and the old claim that the function itself returns that error code is wrong: line 1921 adds outBuffSize without an error check.

name: ZSTD_decompressStream
prose: Precondition: zds is an initialized ZSTD_DStream, input->src and output->dst point to buffers of at least input->size and output->size bytes, input->pos <= input->size, output->pos <= output->size, and in stable output-buffer mode the output buffer is large enough for the frame's declared content size. Postcondition: on a non-error return it advances input->pos and output->pos by the bytes consumed and produced, updates zds's streaming state and expectedOutBuffer, and returns 0 when the frame is fully decoded and all output flushed (releasing the hostage byte by advancing input->pos when it is present), returns 1 when the frame is decoded but output remains unflushed (retaining the last input byte as hostage, decrementing input->pos if not already held) or when the frame is decoded and flushed but the hostage byte cannot be released because input->pos >= input->size, and otherwise returns nextSrcSizeHint (plus ZSTD_blockHeaderSize when the next input is a block, minus the bytes already loaded, zds->inPos) as the size hint for the next call; the code only asserts inPos <= the hint, so a positive value is not established here (in the header-loading path it also sets input->pos = input->size after copying the available bytes into the internal header buffer); on failure it returns a ZSTD error code (ZSTD_isError true), such as srcSize_wrong, dstSize_tooSmall, corruption_detected, frameParameter_windowTooLarge, memory_allocation, noForwardProgress_destFull, noForwardProgress_inputEmpty, or an error propagated from header parsing or block decompression, leaving input->pos and output->pos unchanged for errors raised while processing, whereas the noForwardProgress_destFull and noForwardProgress_inputEmpty errors are raised after input->pos and output->pos have been stored (2243-2253); the caller keeps ownership of both buffers and zds retains its streaming state for the next call.
note: Read zstd_decompress.c:2243-2283. Reviewer claims: round-1 and round-2 (return values: hint, return 1 when hostage cannot be released) RIGHT and already in the prose; two further prose errors found: the hint is not guaranteed positive, and the no-forward-progress errors come after the position update.

name: BDI_SHOW(read_ahead_kb, K(bdi->ra_pages))
prose: Generated function read_ahead_kb_show(dev, attr, buf): precondition is that dev_get_drvdata(dev) yields a valid struct backing_dev_info and buf points to a writable sysfs buffer of at least PAGE_SIZE bytes; postcondition is that it returns the non-negative number of bytes sysfs_emit wrote, namely the value K(bdi->ra_pages) (ra_pages converted to KiB) printed as a decimal long long followed by a newline, taking no locks and holding no references.
note:
Read backing-dev.c:277-287: BDI_SHOW(read_ahead_kb, K(bdi->ra_pages)) generates read_ahead_kb_show returning sysfs_emit(buf, "%lld
", (long long)expr) with bdi from dev_get_drvdata(dev). Prose correct, kept.

name: cma_sysfs_init
prose: Precondition: mm_kobj is a valid kobject and cma_areas[0..cma_area_count-1] are valid CMA areas with names. Postcondition: returns 0 after creating a 'cma' kobject under mm_kobj and one child kobject per CMA area; on any failure it returns a negative error code (e.g. -ENOMEM from kobject_create_and_add or kobject_init_and_add) after putting the root kobject and every child kobject created so far, so no kobject references remain held by the caller.
note: Read cma_sysfs.c:108-146: kobject_create_and_add failure gives -ENOMEM; a kzalloc failure gives -ENOMEM and a kobject_init_and_add failure gives its error (after putting that child); the out label puts the earlier children and the root kobject. Prose correct, kept (the 'e.g. -ENOMEM from kobject_init_and_add' wording is loose but hedged); old contract dropped (the function creates global kobjects, rule 4).

name: isolate_migratepages_block
prose: Precondition: cc points to an initialised compact_control for cc->zone with cc->order, cc->mode, cc->gfp_mask, cc->alloc_contig, cc->finish_pageblock, cc->contended and cc->no_set_skip_hint set, low_pfn and end_pfn delimit the PFN range to scan, mode is a valid isolate_mode_t, and the caller holds no lruvec lock and no extra folio references for pages in the range. Postcondition: the function returns 0 on normal completion, -EAGAIN if too many pages are already isolated (cc->nr_migratepages non-zero or MIGRATE_ASYNC), -EINTR if a fatal signal is pending, or -ENOMEM propagated from isolate_or_dissolve_huge_folio; cc->migrate_pfn is set to the resume PFN (clamped so it never exceeds end_pfn), cc->total_migrate_scanned is increased by the number of pages scanned, and every LRU folio it successfully isolates is removed from the LRU (lruvec_del_folio) with the per-node NR_ISOLATED counter increased by folio_nr_pages(folio), while movable-ops pages (isolate_movable_ops_page, goto isolate_success) skip those two steps and huge folios isolated by isolate_or_dissolve_huge_folio are put on cc->migratepages by that helper (isolate_success_no_list); in all cases the isolated folio is on cc->migratepages and cc->nr_migratepages is increased by folio_nr_pages(folio), its reference transferred to the caller (who must migrate it or return it via putback_movable_pages); on failure or abort paths the folio being processed is put back on the LRU and released, pages already isolated are returned via putback_movable_pages with cc->nr_migratepages reset to 0 on the skip_on_failure and -ENOMEM paths, and any held lruvec lru_lock is released with interrupts restored before returning.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function isolate_migratepages_block at compaction.c:837-1308. Reviewer round-15 claim (movable-ops pages jump to isolate_success without the LRU removal and NR_ISOLATED update) is RIGHT (1060-1062 versus 1200-1206); prose corrected. -EAGAIN/-EINTR returns verified at 864, 868, 873, and the fatal_pending path at 922-924.

name: compact_zone
prose: Precondition: the caller passes a compact_control cc whose zone, order, gfp_mask, mode, highest_zoneidx, alloc_flags, whole_zone, direct_compaction and ignore_skip_hint fields are set for a valid zone, whose migratepages list and freepages[] lists are empty, and capc is either NULL or a capture_control whose page is NULL; the caller retains ownership of cc and capc. Postcondition: the function returns a compact_result — if is_via_compact_memory(cc->order) is false and compaction_suit_allocation_order() returns a value other than COMPACT_CONTINUE, that value is returned immediately, before any scanner PFN, counter or list state is touched; otherwise it returns COMPACT_CONTENDED (on ISOLATE_ABORT, or on a migrate_pages -ENOMEM when the scanners have not met), COMPACT_SUCCESS (when capc captured a page), or the value of the final compact_finished() call — and on every path that gets past the allocation-order check cc->migratepages is empty, all isolated free pages have been released so cc->nr_freepages is 0, cc->total_migrate_scanned and cc->total_free_scanned have been counted, and the zone's compact_cached_free_pfn and compact_cached_migrate_pfn[] are updated only along those paths.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function compact_zone at compaction.c:2542-2778. Read its returns/gotos: early return of compaction_suit_allocation_order's value (2573-2574, before any scanner state is touched), ISOLATE_ABORT and migrate_pages -ENOMEM with unmet scanners giving COMPACT_CONTENDED (2649-2653, 2692-2694), COMPACT_SUCCESS when capc captured a page (2726), the compact_finished result otherwise, and the common out label (2750-2777). Reviewer claims (the early return skips PFN updates and counters) RIGHT and already reflected in the prose ('on every path that gets past the allocation-order check'). Prose kept.

name: try_to_compact_pages
prose: Precondition: ac points to a valid alloc_context whose zonelist, highest_zoneidx and nodemask are initialized, capc points to a valid capture_control, and gfp_mask, order, alloc_flags and prio are valid compaction parameters. Postcondition: the function returns COMPACT_SKIPPED immediately, without touching capc, when gfp_compaction_allowed(gfp_mask) is false; otherwise it walks the zones of ac->zonelist up to ac->highest_zoneidx filtered by ac->nodemask, skipping zones rejected by the cpuset check (cpusets enabled and alloc_flags has ALLOC_CPUSET) and, when prio > MIN_COMPACT_PRIORITY, zones for which compaction_deferred(zone, order) holds (folding COMPACT_DEFERRED into the running result), sets capc->zone to the zone only around each compact_zone_order call and resets it to NULL right after, forces that zone's status to COMPACT_SUCCESS when capc->page is set, and returns the maximum status seen so far (COMPACT_SKIPPED if no zone was compacted); the loop stops after a COMPACT_SUCCESS (after calling compaction_defer_reset(zone, order, false) for that zone), otherwise it calls defer_compaction(zone, order) for zones that returned COMPACT_COMPLETE or COMPACT_PARTIAL_SKIPPED when prio != COMPACT_PRIO_ASYNC, and it breaks out when prio == COMPACT_PRIO_ASYNC and need_resched() or when fatal_signal_pending(current); on every return path after the first zone is handed to compact_zone_order capc->zone has been reset to NULL (the early COMPACT_SKIPPED return leaves capc untouched) and no zone reference is retained by the caller.
note: Slice cut the head (name outside slice); real function try_to_compact_pages at compaction.c:2814-2889 read in full. Reviewer round-15 claim (capc->zone is not reset on the early gfp_compaction_allowed return, which leaves capc untouched) is RIGHT (2822-2823); prose corrected.
